meta.name: English
language.label: Language
watch.note: Reads the file as it is written: each record is checked as it lands, and what happens at the tail is said as the verifier names it. A watch holds every record it checked in memory and stops itself at its limit; it never writes the file. To read the file whole — boots, spans, the report — stop and open it.
watch.kind.shrunk: the unfinished tail was cut — a writer resuming after a crash does this; waiting for its recovery records
watch.kind.recovered: the writer resumed and recorded the cut tail
watch.snapshot.no_link: the header chain does not link
watch.snapshot.ok: Over the {records} checked so far, each links to the one before it; {head}.{anchored} Bodies are not walked here — open the file for that.
watch.snapshot.anchor_in: The anchor's head is in it.
watch.snapshot.anchor_out: The anchor's head is not reached.
watch.snapshot.head: head {head}…
scitt.note: A statement someone published about this chain — its head, and in a v3 statement the root over every record up to it — signed under their key. Checked against a key you choose: the key is what you trust, so it is yours to pick. A statement says the chain had this head when it was signed, by whoever holds that key. Whether a transparency service registered it is that service's receipt, not checked here.
scitt.refused.why: A refusal names the check that failed, not why — a statement about another chain, a damaged file and one signed with another key are refused alike.
scitt.accepted: Accepted: signed under this key, committing to this chain's head at #{seq}{range}, a {version} statement.{root}{grown}
scitt.accepted.root_recomputed: Its root over records #0–#{last} was recomputed here and matches.
scitt.accepted.root_carried: It carries a root, not recomputed here.
scitt.accepted.grown: The chain has grown since: it now holds {records}.
scitt.accepted.id: Statement id {id}… — what to refer to it by.
scitt.refusal.chain_too_short: this chain is shorter than the statement's range
scitt.refusal.content_type_unknown: not a statement construction the package knows
scitt.refusal.detached_payload: the payload is not inside the statement
scitt.refusal.format_id_mismatch: not a statement about a PALA-1 chain
scitt.refusal.head_mismatch: it commits to another head than this chain has there
scitt.refusal.indefinite_length_map: written in a CBOR form the package does not accept
scitt.refusal.key_type_mismatch: the key is not of the type its algorithm needs
scitt.refusal.non_deterministic_encoding: not in the one encoding the package accepts
scitt.refusal.payload_keys_mismatch: its payload does not hold what its construction says
scitt.refusal.protected_header_malformed: its signed header cannot be read
scitt.refusal.protected_labels_mismatch: its signed header holds other labels than the construction's
scitt.refusal.range_invalid: the range it reports is not a range
scitt.refusal.repeated_key: a key appears twice in one of its maps
scitt.refusal.root_mismatch: its root is not this chain's root over the same records
scitt.refusal.signature_invalid: the signature does not verify under this key
scitt.refusal.trailing_bytes: bytes follow the statement, outside what was signed
scitt.refusal.unprotected_header_malform: its unsigned header cannot be read
scitt.refusal.unsupported_alg: signed with an algorithm the package does not verify
bundle.note: An evidence bundle: the selected records, an inclusion proof for each one a proof window covers, the verification and the anchor, in one tar a recipient re-checks from the specification alone (check_bundle.py, in Auditor's repository, does it with Python's standard library). Derived and unsigned — the chain stays authoritative. A selection, at most {max} records: an excerpt around a finding, not the archive.
bundle.refused.empty: the file holds no records to bundle
bundle.refused.wide: a bundle selects at most {max} records, and #{from}–#{to} is {width} — narrow the range around what is to be shown, or export the records
bundle.line.none_proven: , none with an inclusion proof — the chain carries no proof window over them; the verification inside still covers them
bundle.line.some_proven: , {proofs} of them with an inclusion proof — the others lie outside any proof window the chain carries
bundle.line.head: Head {head}….
bundle.line.inconsistent: The bundle holds {records}{proofs}. Its verification says the file is not consistent — bundled as it is, for inspection.{head}
bundle.line.consistent: Its verification says the file is consistent.
proof.note: Shows that this chain's first records, as they are now, are a prefix of the whole — without the records, from two roots and a handful of hashes. The roots are derived from the headers, and the proof is unsigned: it shows two roots agree, never where a root came from. Keep the proof with the root you took when you archived or handed over a prefix; checked later against the grown chain, it shows whether the prefix is still the same records.
proof.count.not_number: a count of records, a whole number
proof.count.zero: a prefix holds at least one record
proof.made: The first {first} are a prefix of the first {second}: root {from}… → {to}…, a path of {path}{verifies}
proof.made.does_not: — and it does not verify, which the package should never produce.
proof.check.cannot: this chain holds {records}, fewer than {n}: it cannot say
proof.check.holds: this chain's root over its first {count} is the proof's {which} root
proof.check.differs: this chain's root over its first {count} is not the proof's {which} root — those {n} are not the records the proof was made over
proof.check.path_ok: the proof's path connects its own two roots — which says nothing of where they came from
proof.check.path_bad: the proof's path does not connect its two roots: it shows nothing
diagnosis.truncated_tail.title: The file ends mid-record
diagnosis.truncated_tail.look.1: Whether the writing process was still running when this file was copied — a live log ends mid-record by definition, and the rule is to verify a copy rather than the file being written.
diagnosis.truncated_tail.look.2: The host's own logs around the end of this file, for a restart or a power loss.
diagnosis.truncated_tail.look.3: Whether a later segment of the same chain exists; a truncated tail is often only the end of one file, not the end of the history.
diagnosis.prefix_absent.title: The chain does not start at its beginning
diagnosis.prefix_absent.look.1: Whether an earlier segment of this chain exists — the first record here is not a GENESIS, so something precedes it.
diagnosis.prefix_absent.look.2: How this file was extracted: a copy taken from an offset, or a partial transfer, produces exactly this.
diagnosis.seq_gap.title: A sequence number is missing
diagnosis.seq_gap.look.1: Whether records were dropped under load — the writer records shedding explicitly, so look for a SHED record near the gap.
diagnosis.seq_gap.look.2: Whether two segments were concatenated with something missing between them.
diagnosis.chain_break.title: A record does not name its predecessor
diagnosis.chain_break.look.1: The record at the break and the one before it — everything earlier still verifies, so the history up to that point stands.
diagnosis.chain_break.look.2: Whether two chains were spliced: a break at a boundary where the boot identifier also changes is a different situation from one inside a boot.
diagnosis.record_violation.title: One record breaks a rule the format requires
diagnosis.record_violation.look.1: The named record: the verifier's finding is about that one record. Whether the chain around it holds is question one's answer, above — this card does not claim it.
diagnosis.record_violation.look.2: Which writer version produced it — a violation confined to one record is more often a writer defect than anything else.
diagnosis.unanchored_tail.title: Records exist past the anchored head
diagnosis.unanchored_tail.look.1: When the anchor was last written — records after it are not evidence of a problem, only of an anchor that has not caught up.
diagnosis.unanchored_tail.look.2: The anchor's own cadence: if it lags routinely, this is the normal state of the system rather than an event.
diagnosis.not_a_container.title: This file does not begin with a PALA-1 record
diagnosis.not_a_container.look.1: Whether the right file was opened — its first bytes are not the record magic, so nothing at the start of it was written by a PALA-1 writer.
diagnosis.not_a_container.look.2: Whether the chain is inside something else: an archive, an export, or a transfer that added a header of its own.
diagnosis.empty_container.title: The file holds no records
diagnosis.empty_container.look.1: Whether the right file was opened — nothing in it contradicts the format, and nothing in it is a chain, so there was nothing to check.
diagnosis.empty_container.look.2: Whether the writer had started: a log created and never written to looks exactly like this, and so does a copy taken before the first record was flushed.
diagnosis.declared_continuation.title: A later segment, by its own first record's declaration
diagnosis.declared_continuation.look.1: Why question one still answers no: this file starts after the chain's beginning, and a file taken on its own cannot prove what came before it. For a rotated chain that is its ordinary shape.
diagnosis.declared_continuation.look.2: The segments manifest named under this card — whether it was found, and whether it names the same predecessor the first record declares.
diagnosis.declared_continuation.look.3: The declared retention floor on the first record: a prefix removed under a declared retention policy is expected; one removed sooner than the floor is worth asking about.
diagnosis.declared_continuation.look.4: The earlier segments themselves, if this review needs the whole history — the first record says how many records came before it.
diagnosis.continuation_contradicts_manif: The segment's declaration and the manifest beside it disagree
Whether the manifest belongs to this chain — one copied from another deployment, or from another rotation of the same one, disagrees in exactly this way.
Where this file and the manifest each came from, and when; the manifest's path and the digest of the bytes the verifier read are named under this card.
The previous segment itself, if it is still held: the hash of its last record is what both the declaration and the manifest claim to name.
diagnosis.replaced_or_rolled_back.title: The anchored head is not in this chain
diagnosis.replaced_or_rolled_back.look.1: Whether the anchor belongs to this chain at all — an anchor from a different deployment produces this exactly.
diagnosis.replaced_or_rolled_back.look.2: Whether the file was restored from a backup taken before the anchored head.
diagnosis.replaced_or_rolled_back.look.3: The anchor source that answered: a stale entry in a store is far more common than a replaced log, and the provenance panel names which source it came from.
diagnosis.unknown.title: A failure this build has no guidance for
diagnosis.unknown.look.1: The verifier's own description below — it is authoritative, and this application simply has nothing to add to it.
diagnosis.unknown.look.2: Whether this reader is older than the writer that produced the file; a newer verifier may name a pattern this one does not know.
advisory.mono_regression_in_boot.title: The monotonic clock moved backwards within a boot
advisory.mono_regression_in_boot.note: Monotonic time is not supposed to go back inside one boot. Worth knowing before reading any duration from this stretch.
advisory.wall_regression_in_boot.title: The wall clock moved backwards within a boot
advisory.wall_regression_in_boot.note: A correction, a manual change and a synchronisation step all look like this. Chain order is unaffected — it was never based on the wall clock.
advisory.mid_boot_time_trust_change.titl: The clock's trust level changed mid-boot
advisory.mid_boot_time_trust_change.note: Records before and after the change carry different qualifications on their wall-clock times, so a single sentence about this boot's timing would not be true of all of it.
advisory.anchor_never_written.title: No anchor record was ever written
advisory.anchor_never_written.note: Nothing in this chain records a head having been anchored. Question two can still be answered from an anchor kept outside the file.
advisory.span_unclosed.title: A span was opened and never closed
advisory.span_unclosed.note: First-class evidence rather than a fault: a span left open is what an interrupted operation looks like, and the records it opened are still in the file.
advisory.span_unopened.title: A span was closed without an opening record
advisory.span_unopened.note: The opening record is not in this file. An earlier segment of the same chain is the usual explanation.
advisory.reference_unresolved.title: A record points at a record that is not here
advisory.reference_unresolved.note: The target may be in another segment of the same chain. Unresolved is not the same as missing.
advisory.reference_hash_mismatch.title: A reference names a record whose hash does not match
advisory.reference_hash_mismatch.note: Two things that should agree do not: the reference carries a hash, and the record it names hashes to something else.
advisory.ack_target_not_a_candidate.titl: An acknowledgement points at something that is not an incident candidate
advisory.ack_target_not_a_candidate.note: The oversight loop expects an acknowledgement to name a candidate. This one names a different kind of record.
advisory.shred_target_unresolved.title: A key-shred record names a record that is not here
advisory.shred_target_unresolved.note: The target may be in another segment. The shred itself is recorded either way.
advisory.shred_target_key_mismatch.title: A key-shred record names a record encrypted under a different key
advisory.shred_target_key_mismatch.note: The shred claims a key that the named record does not use.
advisory.tool_target_not_a_call.title: A tool result or loop guard names a record that is not a tool call
advisory.tool_target_not_a_call.note: The reference resolves, and its hash matches, but the record it names is of another kind than the result or guard expects.
advisory.continuation_malformed.title: A segment continuation record is missing a declared field
advisory.continuation_malformed.note: A SEGMENT_CONTINUATION should carry four declarations at fixed widths. This one does not, so nothing it declares is shown.
advisory.continuation_predecessor_mismat: A continuation declares a predecessor its own header does not name
The declared previous head and the record's own prev_hash should be the same value. They are not.
advisory.continuation_index_not_increasi: Each continuation declares its segment's place in the chain; a later one declares the same place or an earlier one.
advisory.continuation_index_gap.title: Segment indices skip a number
advisory.continuation_index_gap.note: With the whole chain present from its beginning, consecutive continuations should declare consecutive segment numbers. These do not.
advisory.continuation_prior_root_mismatc: A continuation declares a root the records before it do not produce
The reader recomputed the root of every record before the continuation, and it differs from the root the writer declared at the cut.
advisory.boot_ended_without_close.title: A boot ended without its writer closing it
advisory.boot_ended_without_close.note: The writer marked this boot's start (WRITER_OPEN) and the next boot begins with no WRITER_CLOSE before it: the process was stopped without closing — a crash, a kill, a power cut. The chain itself is whole.
advisory.reports_refused.title: Reports to a reporting route did not get in
advisory.reports_refused.note: The serving layer refused or rejected reports on this route and wrote down how many. For this run, the absence of reported events is not evidence that nothing happened. Not who tried, and not what the reports held — the serving layer did not learn that.
advisory.unknown.note: This build has no description for this advisory code. The items below are the package's own.
verdict.q1.question: Is what I hold internally consistent?
verdict.q1.basis: Proved — hash chain and body digests, no key required
verdict.q1.mismatch: The headers link, but {where} no longer match the body digest their own header carries.
verdict.q1.not_a_container: This file does not begin with a PALA-1 record. It is not a chain, so nothing in it was linked or checked.
verdict.q1.empty: This file holds no records, so nothing in it was linked or checked.
verdict.q1.linked: {records}, each linked to the one before it and matching its own body digest.
verdict.q1.not_whole: {records} read and linked, but the file is not whole.
verdict.q1.unguided: {linked} The verifier also reported a finding this build has no guidance for.
verdict.q1.no_hold: {records} read; the chain does not hold.
verdict.q2.question: Is what I hold all of it?
verdict.q2.no_anchor: Not checked — no anchor was supplied.

verdict.q2.none_answered.one: Not checked — {n} anchor source was consulted and none answered.
verdict.q2.none_answered.other: Not checked — {n} anchor sources were consulted and none answered.

verdict.q2.basis.none: No answer without an anchor from outside this file
verdict.q2.empty: This file holds no records, so nothing was checked against the head held by {from}.
verdict.q2.complete.host_local: Complete to the head held by {from}. At tier A a head kept on the same host as the log can be rewritten with it — this is complete against that store, nothing more.
verdict.q2.complete: Complete to the head held by {from}.

verdict.q2.lag.one: {n} record sits beyond the head held by {from}.
verdict.q2.lag.other: {n} records sit beyond the head held by {from}.

verdict.q2.not_in_chain: The head held by {from} does not name a record in this chain.
verdict.q3.question: Did this history exist at time T?
verdict.q3.clock.changed: the writer's clock, which changed status mid-chain ({clocks})
verdict.q3.answer: No external evidence in this file. Order is proved; the times are what {clock} recorded.
boot.q1.basis: Proved — hash chain, no key required
boot.q3.basis: Recorded — the writer's clock, until a witness says otherwise
boot.footnote.no_shell: Running in a browser without the desktop shell, so there is no session token and no sidecar. Use `pnpm tauri dev` to run the whole application.
boot.footnote.failed: The sidecar did not answer: {detail}. Check that Python is on PATH and that the sidecar package is installed.
boot.footnote.verified: The panels above attest that this check was run against this file, with this anchor profile, at this time. They certify nothing.
boot.footnote.idle: Opening a chain reports what it is. Nothing on this screen is a verification result.
boot.choice.no_shell: Choosing a file needs the desktop shell. Run `pnpm tauri dev`.

boot.choice.extra.one: {n} file was dropped; only the first was opened. Several files as one chain is not supported yet.
boot.choice.extra.other: {n} files were dropped; only the first was opened. Several files as one chain is not supported yet.

health.note: About the record itself — its clock, its boots, its anchors, its warnings — never about what the model did. It describes and draws no line: advisory, and it does not affect the verdict.
health.basis.monotonic: the writer's monotonic clock — within one boot only
health.basis.recorded: recorded — the writer's wall clock, a claim
health.step.step: the wall clock moved {delta} against the monotonic clock in one record
health.step.regression: the wall clock read {delta} earlier than on the record before
health.step.slew: the wall clock drifted {delta} against the monotonic clock over several records
health.life.stopped: opened{by} at #{open}, never closed — the process was stopped before the next boot (a crash, a kill, a power cut); advisory, the chain is whole
health.life.last: opened{by} at #{open}, not closed yet — still being written, or stopped for good; the chain cannot tell which
health.drift.head: Clock drift per boot, {note}.
health.drift.none: {head} No boot has two records to take a slope over.
health.anchors.gap: {anchors}, at most {gap} apart — an external witness of each would date any record here to within that
health.gap.negative: Boot {before} begins {span} earlier, by the writer's clock, than boot {after} ended.
health.gap: {span} between boot {after} and boot {before}, by the writer's clock.
record.source.telemetry.note: written from an exported telemetry span when the export arrived, not at the call — its place in the chain and its time are the export's, not the call's
record.writer_open: the writer's own record: it started writing this boot and will mark its close. Its detail names the writer and its version
record.writer_close: the writer's own last record: it closed this boot. A head taken before it is the head of a chain one record shorter — anchor after the writer stops
record.shred.note: as the writer declared it when it noted the key's destruction — whether those records exist and carried that key is the chain's answer under “shredded”, not this note's
record.refused.note: for this run, the absence of reported events is not evidence that nothing happened. Counts of requests since the serving layer started, as they stood when this was written — not who sent them, not what they held, and no count of tool events
record.refused.counts: {empty} refused with no credential, {wrong} refused with a wrong one, {rejected} read and rejected, {accepted} accepted
record.ack.cross_boot: acknowledged in a later boot — no latency is computed across a restart
record.ack.before: the writer's clock puts the ack {span} before the candidate
report.attestation: An attestation that this check was run against this file, with this anchor, at this time — not a certification.
report.health.trust: , {n} with a change of clock trust
witness.limits: The witness log shows that this desk saw this head at this point in its own sequence, and makes a later change to an entry visible. It shows nothing about the world: its clock is this machine's, a log cut at its end still links, and whoever controls this machine can write a new one. Note its head somewhere else to make a cut visible.
witness.not_written: Not written to the witness log: {error}
witness.written: Written to this desk's witness log as entry {n}.
witness.broken: The witness log does not link at line {line}: {reason}. {before}; nothing is added to it until it does.
witness.empty: The witness log has no entries yet.

witness.links.one: {n} entry links, each to the one before it.
witness.links.other: {n} entries link, each to the one before it.

export.summary.consistent: The export's summary: consistent — the headers link, the container parses to its end, and every body matches its digest.{records} Completeness was not checked.
export.summary.unknown: The export's summary does not say whether the file is consistent.{records}
export.reason.not_parsed: the container does not parse to its end
export.reason.body.one: the body of record {seqs} does not match the digest its header carries
export.reason.body.many: {n} record bodies ({seqs}) do not match the digest their header carries
export.reason.no_link: the header chain does not link
export.reason.unnamed: for a reason the summary does not name
export.summary.inconsistent: The export's summary says the file is not consistent: {why}.{records} The export was saved as it is — it is a view of that file, for examining it.
export.note: A readable view of the binary log — derived, never authoritative: it carries no signature and enters no hash. Its summary line describes the whole file, a range included, and reads no anchor, so completeness is not checked. Whatever is concluded from it is concluded about the record each line names, and checked there.
range.not_number: the {which} bound is not a record number: {text}
range.backwards: the range starts at #{from}, after its end at #{to}
set.consistent: Consistent: every segment present ({present} of {total}) holds from its declared start and agrees with the manifest, and every seam links.
set.inconsistent: Not consistent: a segment present does not hold, or does not agree with the manifest, or a seam does not link — see the segments below.
set.complete: Complete: nothing the manifest lists is missing, and the set starts at its first record.
set.incomplete.inconsistent: Not complete, since it is not consistent.

set.incomplete.absent.one: Not complete: one segment the manifest lists is not here. What it held is not claimed; deletion under a retention policy leaves a set this way.
set.incomplete.absent.other: Not complete: {n} segments the manifest lists are not here. What they held is not claimed; deletion under a retention policy leaves a set this way.

set.incomplete.start: Not complete: the set does not start at the chain's first record — its beginning is declared, not here.
set.segment.head: head {head}…
set.segment.declared: listed, not here — declared {declared}; not here to check
set.segment.head_differs: its last record is not the head the manifest gives
set.segment.no_seam: does not link to the segment before it
set.segment.live: the writer's live segment, not yet in the manifest
prov.note.answered: Answered. This is the head the check was made against.
prov.note.not_reached: Not consulted — an earlier source had already answered, so the {kind} source was never asked.
f7.unrecognised: chain-checked, not interpretable by this verifier version
manifest.none: No segments manifest could be looked for, so the first record's declaration stands unconfirmed.
manifest.matches: This verdict also rests on {at}: it names the same predecessor the first record declares.
manifest.contradicts: This verdict also rests on {at}: it does not name the predecessor the first record declares.
manifest.not_read: No segments manifest was read at {path}, so the first record's declaration stands unconfirmed.
manifest.set_aside: The segments manifest at {path} was read and set aside, so the first record's declaration stands unconfirmed.
manifest.unknown: This verdict also rests on {at}; this build has no sentence for the status "{status}".
browse.extent.closed: opened and closed within this file
browse.extent.unclosed: opened, never closed by its owner
browse.extent.began_earlier: closed here; it began before this file
browse.extent.spans_file: neither end is in this file
browse.trust_changed: the clock's trust changed during this boot ({clocks}), so no single statement about wall time covers all of it
browse.recovered: this boot recovered a truncated tail at record #{seq}
nearest.not_ordered: In this file the writer's clock does not follow the chain's order, so nearest by the clock is not a position in the history.
nearest.stepped: The writer's clock stepped during this record's boot.

nearest.equal.one: {n} other record is equally near; the earliest in the chain is shown.
nearest.equal.other: {n} other records are equally near; the earliest in the chain is shown.

rail.pins.none: No external witness in this file.
rail.down.all: {span} · the writer was down for all of them
rail.down.some: {span} · the writer was down for part of them
chain.empty: No chain open. Nothing on this screen is a verification result.
chain.not_a_file: {path} could not be read as a file: {detail}
chain.changed: The file changed since it was opened, so nothing here describes it any more: {detail}
hex.no_header: The package does not interpret this header, so no field is named: the bytes are shown as the file holds them.
hex.no_tlvs: The package gives no TLV layout for this body; its bytes are shown as stored, unnamed.
hex.truncated: The first {shown} of the body's {total} bytes are shown; the rest are in the file, not drawn here.
hex.uncovered: A byte no span covers is shown unnamed: the package names TLV values, not the bytes that introduce them.
filter.not_loaded: the {noun} list has not loaded, so "{chip}" cannot be resolved
filter.no_match: no {noun} in this file starts with {prefix}
filter.ambiguous: {prefix} matches {n} in this file — type more of it
filter.empty_range: from: is after to: — the range holds no day
save.print_opened: The report opened in a window of its own; the print dialog there can save it as PDF.
save.saved: Saved to {path} — SHA-256 {sha}, written beside it as {digest}; check with: sha256sum -c {digest}
session.no_shell: not running inside the desktop shell

records.unsearched.one: {n} record matching the other filters has an encrypted body and was not searched for this text.
records.unsearched.other: {n} records matching the other filters have encrypted bodies and were not searched for this text.

origin.digest_note: the writer's claim. Writers from palimpsests 0.15 digest the canonical (RFC 8785) form, so the same configuration digests differently across the 0.14 → 0.15 upgrade: a new origin there is not by itself a change of configuration — the boot's WRITER_OPEN names the writer's version
rail.bad_timeline: the rail needs a day-aligned wall timeline, got axis={axis} align={align}
search.quote_it: to search detail text, put it in double quotes
search.bad_time: "{text}" is not a time jump — write @2026-08-06T22:41Z
search.open_quote: a quote is not closed — free text goes between two double quotes
search.empty_quotes: the quotes are empty — there is no text to search for
search.too_long: the quoted text is longer than {max} characters
search.not_chip: "{token}" is not #<seq> or a filter chip — {hint}
search.unknown_chip: "{key}:" is not a chip this build reads — it reads {keys}
search.twice: "{key}:" appears twice — one value per chip
search.bad_day: "{chip}" — a date is YYYY-MM-DD, a real UTC day
search.help.time: go to the record nearest that time by the writer's clock — a claim; no zone is UTC
search.help.kind: list only that kind; also type:, tier:, source:, outcome:
search.help.ids: list only that boot or span, by the start of its id
search.help.days: list only those days, by the writer's clock
search.help.text: list only records whose detail contains the phrase; one phrase, any case
search.help.slash: key: jump to this search field
search.help.jk: keys: next and previous record in the list

anchors.title: Anchor profiles
anchors.note: An anchor is the chain's head kept somewhere other than the log: in a file on another disk, in this machine's secret store, on a hardware token, or written down when the log was handed over. Only against an anchor can question two be answered: a log whose end was cut off still links, but its head no longer matches the anchor. A profile is the list of places to look, tried in order; the first that answers is used, and the provenance panel says which one did. A profile keeps where to look, never a secret.
anchors.none_yet: No profiles yet. Until there is one, question two stays not checked.
anchors.name: Name
anchors.order: Sources are asked in this order. The first that answers is used; the ones before it are reported as tried.
anchors.kind.file.note: A file the writer's anchor step wrote, on a disk or share the log's own machine cannot change. Read each time a check uses this profile.
anchors.kind.keychain.note: Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain or the Secret Service, under an account name you choose. On the same machine as the log, it is completeness against that store and no more.
anchors.kind.manual.note: A head handed over on paper or in a message when the log was handed over: 64 hexadecimal characters. Copy it, do not retype it — a head with one wrong character names no record.
anchors.kind.pkcs11.note: A head kept on a hardware token. The token's PIN is not kept here: it is in this machine's secret store, under the account named below.
anchors.field.head: Head
anchors.field.pin_account: PIN's account in the secret store
anchors.saved: Saved the profile {name}; it is chosen for the next check.
anchors.name.long: a name is one line of at most {max} characters
anchors.name.none: “none” is the no-anchor profile; choose another name
anchors.name.taken: there is already a profile named {name}
anchors.need.source: a profile needs at least one source

anchors.keychain.seed_note: To put a head into the secret store under this account, paste it here. It is stored as typed, so copy it from where it was kept rather than retyping it.
anchors.keychain.stored: Stored the head under the account {account}.
app.health.by_origin_note: The chain cut where the declared model, configuration or role changes, as the package reads it, with the SAFETY records written under each stretch. Counts and ranges are by proved order; what was loaded is the writer's declaration. Side by side, not explained: a difference between two stretches says when, never why.
